target_customer: Home inspectors (software and lead supply) and real estate, lending and insurance firms that buy inspections, valuations and underwriting data
problem: Home inspections are inconsistent, slow to schedule and deliver little structured data for buyers, agents and lenders.
business_model: Marketplace and services take rate on inspections plus software for inspectors, expanding to valuations and appraisal services

founders.name: Josh Jensen
founders.background_notes: From the YC company page, which lists operations roles at Series A startups. Education not stated.

founders.name: Denis Bellavance
previous_startups: Peach (food delivery, Seattle; outcome not found)
founders.background_notes: From the YC company page. Education not stated.

investors: HSB Fund of Munich Re Ventures

technical_complexity.rationale: Scheduling, report generation and marketplace software on standard web stack; the hard part was operations and inspector supply, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Two sided supply of inspectors could build a local network effect, but inspectors multi-home and report software is commoditized.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied the platform in sources found. Inspectify itself acquired Aloft and Joule in 2025.

market_need_then: The 2020 housing boom and growth of iBuyers and online lenders created demand for fast, standardized inspections and property data.

branding.domain_note: Company site is inspectify.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Hummingbird made of three polygons for agents, buyers and inspectors, introduced in a July 2021 rebrand

rebrands.why: Company said it wanted an identity that better represented its mission and customers

brand_strength.rationale: Only the company's own rebrand post was found; no press on the brand itself or community evidence.

outcome_analysis: Inspectify raised a seed in November 2020 and an 8 million Series A in November 2021, then cut 16 staff in October 2022 amid the housing slowdown and raised a smaller round in 2023. It reported nearly 12 million in gross revenue for 2024 and made two acquisitions in 2025, so it stayed independent and expanded toward valuations and appraisals.
notes: Competitors list left empty: Spectora, HomeGauge and ISN appear in directory pages but none of those sources is dated near the 2020 batch. The 2023 round was seen via the GeekWire headline in search results; stage label not stated so recorded as other. ZoomInfo lists 5.3M in 2024 led by Munich Re Ventures and another profile lists a 13M Series A in 2022, both unverified and not recorded. Layoff of 16 employees in October 2022 reported by a Business Journal item in search results.
